findings.issue: PROP-005(b) justifies the manual-read gate's tractability by claiming each of the four WORKER files is 'under 100 lines'. That is false for run.sh, which is 107 lines (verified: the file's last line is line 107). The other three are genuinely small (_instance_paths.sh=17, producer.sh=71, monitor.sh=75). This is an immaterial overstatement — a 107-line shell script is still a fully tractable manual read, so the two-tier gate remains executable — but the specific numeric claim is inaccurate and should be corrected to 'each ~70-110 lines' or 'each well under 150 lines' to avoid a reviewer flagging the guarantee as fabricated. Does NOT block: the gate mechanism (Phase-3 adversary reads all four WORKER files in full and confirms zero model/provider conditionals of any shape) is coherent and does not depend on the exact <100 boundary.

resolvedFromIteration3: FIND-001 (BLOCKING, verification_tool_mismatch — PROP-005 line-based grep unsound vs multi-line `case`, plus false 'only matches inside constructs / out of scope by construction' prose): RESOLVED. verification-architecture.md:24 now explicitly and honestly concedes 'A perfectly sound static check is not achievable with grep on shell source' and replaces the sole-grep gate with an explicit TWO-TIER method: (a) a labelled HEURISTIC pre-check grep ('a fast smell-test, not proof'), and (b) an AUTHORITATIVE full manual read of all four WORKER files by the Phase-3 fresh-context adversary that confirms 'zero conditionals of any shape (single- or multi-line if/case) branch on model/provider identity'. The prior overclaiming prose ('only matches inside constructs', 'out of scope by construction') is deleted. Confirmed executable: clip-cli.sh:22-25 shows the exact multi-line `case "${1:-}" in` form the old grep would miss, and the manual read (b) — not (a) — is what gates Phase-3 PASS, so the evasion path is closed. Coherent, not hand-wavy.

FIND-002 (MAJOR, spec_gap — REQ-005 'only env vars differ' contradicted by clip-cli.sh hardcoding `claude`/`--model sonnet`): RESOLVED. behavioral-spec.md:66-73 adds an explicit REQ-005 carve-out naming clip-cli.sh as the per-instance persistent-loop LAUNCHER (verified: clip-cli.sh:15 hardcodes the `claude` binary, clip-cli.sh:33 hardcodes `--model sonnet`), correctly scoping the agnosticism guarantee to the four WORKER scripts only and stating a self-funded ClawRouter instance needs a DIFFERENT launcher (future clip-cli-clawrouter.sh) tracked out of scope. behavioral-spec.md:28-31 (Out of scope) now explicitly defers 'Building a second, ClawRouter-specific persistent-loop LAUNCHER (analogous to clip-cli.sh)' to follow-on `clip-loop-clawrouter-provision`. Carve-out is logically coherent and NON-VACUOUS: REQ-005 still forbids any model/provider conditional inside producer/run/monitor/_instance_paths (a `case "$PROVIDER" in claude)...` in run.sh would still fail the manual-read gate), so it does not define away every possible violation — it only excludes the launcher layer, which is legitimately per-instance by design.

Proof-obligation table has NO orphans: REQ-001..008 each map to exactly one PROP-001..008 and every PROP-001..008 maps to exactly one requirement (one-to-one, verification-architecture.md:20-27).

PROP-004 (verification-architecture.md:23) stands alone coherently: resolves paths for instance-name list ('', myclaude, clawrouter, clawrouter-2) and asserts all 4xN path sets pairwise disjoint (set-based, not eyeballing) — a real, executable distinctness check scoped to the default (unset EARN_LEDGER) derivation, matching REQ-004's note.

REQ-005 currently HOLDS for the WORKER layer as written: run.sh sources _instance_paths.sh (run.sh:20) and its `.claude/skills/...` occurrences (run.sh:25-26) are path literals, not model/provider branches; producer.sh:18 sources it too; no conditional in any of the three impure workers branches on model/provider identity.

No other requirement or PROP references clip-cli.sh in a way that contradicts the REQ-005 carve-out; the only two mentions (REQ-005 carve-out, Out-of-scope) are mutually consistent.
